name: Pagan Kingdom
summary: The first kingdom to unify the Irrawaddy valley of Myanmar. Its kings built more than 10,000 Buddhist temples on the plain of Bagan.

knownFor.label: Temples of Bagan
knownFor.note: Over 10,000 Buddhist temples were built; more than 2,000 still stand.

knownFor.label: Burmese script
knownFor.note: The Burmese alphabet developed here from the Mon script.

knownFor.label: Ananda Temple
knownFor.note: A great white temple built under King Kyansittha.

location.value: The Irrawaddy valley of central Myanmar, centred on the city of Pagan (Bagan).

terrain.value: The dry central plain of Myanmar along the Irrawaddy, made fertile by irrigation.

climate.value: The “dry zone”, with low rainfall, so irrigation was essential.

resources.value: Irrigated rice land in the Kyaukse and Minbu districts.

urbanisation.value: Bagan was a royal city surrounded by thousands of temples on a plain of about 100 km².

migration.value: Burman (Bamar) settlers came down from the north and mixed with Pyu and Mon peoples.

economicBase.value: Irrigated rice farming in the Kyaukse and Minbu districts, and religious donations.

tradeRoutes.value: River trade down the Irrawaddy and sea trade with India, Sri Lanka and China.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Silver used by weight (the kyat), and rice; land given to temples was tax-free.

inequality.value: Much land given to tax-free monasteries.

governmentType.value: Monarchy ruling a core region directly and outer areas through governors.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

succession.value: Hereditary, but often disputed between royal sons.

institutions.value: Large royal and monastic land grants recorded in stone inscriptions.

eliteConflict.value: Large gifts of tax-free land to monasteries drained royal revenue.

majorWars.value: The Mongol invasions (1277–1287) broke the kingdom’s power.

territoryChange.value: Expanded in the 1050s–60s under Anawrahta to unify the Irrawaddy valley and the coast.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Khmer, the Mon and later the Mongols; ties with Sri Lanka.

inventions.value: Irrigation works, weirs and canals in the dry zone.

scienceEducation.value: Monastic education in Pali and Burmese.

openness.value: Close religious contact with Sri Lanka, the source of its Theravada Buddhism.

religion.value: Theravada Buddhism alongside Mahayana, Hindu and animist practices.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

languageWriting.value: Old Burmese, Mon and Pyu; the Burmese script developed here from the Mon script.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

artsArchitecture.value: Over 10,000 temples were built and over 2,000 remain, including the Ananda and Shwezigon.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

socialStructure.value: King and nobles, monks, free farmers and bonded temple servants.

neighbours.value: The Mon, the Khmer, Sri Lanka, Nanzhao and China.

ideasReligions.value: Theravada Buddhism spread to the village level.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

riseSignals.value: Anawrahta unified the Irrawaddy valley in the 1050s–60s.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

peakPeriod.value: About 1174–1250, under Sithu II and his successors.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

declineSignals.value: Tax-free monastic land drained royal revenue; then the Mongol invasions (1277–1287).
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

outcome.value: The kingdom collapsed in 1287 (its last king was overthrown in 1297); 250 years of fragmentation followed.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lieberman, Strange Parallels vol. 1 (2003)

sources.value: Inscriptions, chronicles. Checked against Wikipedia (“Pagan Kingdom”).
